# Architecture

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## Current Python/Tkinter domain model

### Board, moves and rules

`src/model/game/board.py` owns the current mutable board representation. `src/model/game/move.py`, `validator.py` and `rule.py` provide move actions, checks and composable Python rule evaluation. `src/model/game/manager.py` coordinates the constructed `Configuration`, players, turn state, active clocks, move/result events, quest manager, logs and exports. It exposes `make_move`, `get_valid_moves`, `get_state`, `finish_game` and `transcript` rather than the archived JSON engine's `submit_action` and versioned replay API.

### Supporting state

`src/model/game/timer.py`, `clock_fields.py` and variant clock modules manage countdown and increments. `src/model/game/quest.py`, `quests.py` and `src/model/misc/quest_manager.py` manage executable Python quests and rewards. `src/model/misc/` owns notation, metadata and exporters; `src/model/users/` owns user data. These modules do not implement server-backed authentication or persistence.

### Variants and limitations

`src/games/chess/` and `src/games/checkers/` compose boards, pieces and named Python rules through `build_configuration()`. Checkers currently supplies flying kings, not English-draughts short-range kings. The canonical JSON-driven configuration and immutable transactional engine planned for v1.0.0 are not yet connected to this model; implementing them requires replacing the existing executable-configuration path, not adding a competing engine.

_Source: [0001-components.md](decisions/0001-components.md)_


## Current game configuration and source execution

`src/model/game/games.py` locates the packaged `src/games/` configurations; each game package assembles `Configuration` from Python `board.py`, `rules/`, `pieces/`, `quests/`, `clocks/` and exporter modules. `src/model/game/configuration.py` loads modules with `importlib` and exposes copying/renaming/deletion of configuration directories. `src/model/game/source_validation.py` validates editable Python by executing it, and `src/view/code_editor.py` is reachable from settings. This **is the current implementation**, not the approved target JSON-only model.

Pure helpers from that archived implementation have now been restored as `src/model/game/schema.py`, `conditions.py`, `hooks.py`, `capture_policy.py`, `definition.py` and `snapshot_queries.py`. The current versioned validator loads bundled `config.json` resources through `importlib.resources.files("games")` and a strict bounded directory identifier, **without importing individual game subpackages**. It enforces schema-v2/strict-key/type/bound contracts and returns recursively immutable `GameDefinition` data. Source-controlled JSON for chess and English draughts is present under `src/games/`; both definitions remain `playable: false`. The new `SnapshotQueries` module copies and bounds finite JSON facts, rejects missing/untrusted inputs, and can provide a registered trusted query to `RuleProgram` without mutating session state. `capture_policy.EvaluationBudget` applies shared bounded work reservations with atomic parent/child rejection; `RuleProgram.evaluate` accepts that budget during declarative rule evaluation. `capture_geometry.CaptureEnumerator` enumerates bounded single and sequential captures against an unmodified board projection, including both short-range and flying geometry. `BoardQueries` uses the canonical `Board` and `Piece.getMaxSteps()` interfaces to bind declarative queries and charge shared work; `outcomes.resolve_outcome` resolves permitted terminal proposals deterministically. The active manager still uses executable Python configuration, so these recovered helpers do not establish working JSON-driven game transitions or GUI gameplay. The active desktop runtime does not yet read them. They define bounded JSON validation, trusted read-only condition evaluation and immutable effect proposals; none mutates the board or replaces the active Python-loaded `Configuration` or legacy `GameManager` yet. Replacing that runtime is the next integration boundary.

The archived #405 engine instead used validated schema-versioned JSON definitions, bounded conditions/hooks, immutable snapshots, revisioned actions and event replay. Those capabilities are absent from the present desktop working tree and must be integrated into one authoritative engine before replacing source editing. Requirements and architecture will be updated within #271 as the code is actually changed.

_Source: [0002-configuration.md](decisions/0002-configuration.md)_


## Current application entry, controllers and Tkinter views

`src/chesswithquests/__init__.py` parses `--game` and `--check`, reports available games and invokes the Tkinter application via `view.app.build_application`. `src/controller/controller.py` selects active-player squares, requests legal destinations from the game manager and attempts moves. `src/controller/window_controller.py` tracks application window and status state.

`src/view/app.py` coordinates window construction and game selection, while `game_view.py`, `player_game_view.py`, `player_view.py` and `quest_view.py` render the board and gameplay panels. `settings_dialog.py`, `code_editor.py` and `start_modal.py` handle settings, executable source editing and game selection. The domain is in-memory and uses the old mutable Python-configured manager, rather than the revisioned JSON transition API; full end-to-end widget and package acceptance remains unverified.

_Source: [0003-application.md](decisions/0003-application.md)_


## Documentation, CI and desktop release architecture

`.agents/GOAL.md`, `PLAN.md`, `TODO.md` and `SCRATCHPAD.md` are authored records. `.github/scripts/generate_documents.py` derives generated README from published notes, PRD from approved requests, ARCHITECTURE from accepted decisions, and AGENTS from active rules. Root README/CONTRIBUTING are symlinks. `.agents/architecture/diagrams/` derives Mermaid syntax graphs from tracked files and the actual production Python source.

`.github/` owns source checks, central tests, docs preview/publishing, DarkFactory integration and trusted release controls. `develop` is the integration branch; `main` is the protected release branch. The current `src/` Python package is the only desktop application on this PR; `packages/server/`, `packages/client/` and `packages/native/` belong to #422.

The native `desktop-build.yml` workflow builds four platform artifacts using `package_desktop.py`, verifying copied game resources and frozen process startup. `release.yml` checks the live `main` SHA, resolves PrideVer metadata and checks required binaries/checksums before publication. Python release publication remains disabled until actual platform application acceptance is completed. No released binary is claimed by these source definitions.

_Source: [0004-repository.md](decisions/0004-repository.md)_
